prompt: A news website posts a poll asking, "Should the city build a new stadium?" Anyone visiting the site can click to vote. Of the $5{,}000$ votes, $78$ percent say no. What is the main problem with this poll?

choices.label: Voluntary response bias: people with strong opinions choose to vote
The sample is too small to be useful
Nonresponse bias: people who were chosen refused to answer
The question is worded to push people toward "no"

hint: Who decides whether a person ends up in this sample: the pollster, or the person?

hints.text: Who decides whether a person ends up in this sample: the pollster, or the person?
When people select THEMSELVES, the ones who bother are usually the ones who feel strongly, often negatively.
That is voluntary response bias: choice A.

explanation: Nobody was randomly chosen; visitors chose for themselves whether to vote.
People who feel strongly, especially those who are upset, are far more likely to click. The $78$ percent "no" likely overstates opposition.
This is voluntary response bias. Choice A. (A big sample does not fix a biased method, so B is wrong, and the question wording here is neutral.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Nonresponse vs voluntary response
steps: Nonresponse bias happens when the pollster picks people and some of them refuse.
Voluntary response bias happens when nobody is picked and people volunteer.
Here no one was picked, so it is voluntary response.
